objective: Create a consent-aware, provider-neutral contact and call orchestration layer for insurance leads so River can request immediate or callback-based contact, persist the complete attempt lifecycle, safely hand attempts to a future telephony provider, and reconcile provider outcomes without replacing canonical River CRM identity or coupling the CRM domain to one vendor.

architecture.canonicalRelationship: RiverCrmRelationshipId remains the canonical person/lead relationship identity.
architecture.triggerBoundary: RiverCrmRelationshipEvent with eventType callback-requested remains a CRM lifecycle trigger and audit record, not the telephony attempt state machine.
architecture.attemptBoundary: InsuranceContactAttempt is the canonical provider-neutral execution record for each requested phone/SMS/email contact attempt.
architecture.persistenceBoundary: Contact attempt execution state is persisted additively in RIVER_CRM_DB rather than encoded only inside relationship event metadata.
architecture.providerBoundary: All vendor-specific call creation, authentication, provider request IDs, webhooks, status normalization, retry semantics, and transport behavior live behind an InsuranceContactProvider interface.
architecture.consentBoundary: No attempt may be prepared for transport when canonical channel consent is not granted or when doNotContact is true.
architecture.orchestrationBoundary: The orchestration service owns validation, eligibility, attempt creation, state transitions, idempotency intent, provider invocation, provider-result normalization, and persistence sequencing.
architecture.uiBoundary: Private River OS may later request a callback/contact attempt through a same-origin private action. Public quote intake does not receive telephony controls in INS-002.
architecture.productionBoundary: No production migration, deployment, provider account setup, purchased phone number, provider secret, or live call occurs without a later explicit authorization.

coreDecisions: Do not overload river_crm_relationship_events with call execution lifecycle.
Do not use provider call IDs as River identity.
Do not select a telephony vendor in the foundational slices.
Persist durable contact-attempt lifecycle before implementing a real provider adapter.
Treat consent/suppression as a hard orchestration prerequisite rather than a UI-only warning.
Keep callback-requested as an auditable trigger event that can be associated with a resulting contact attempt.
Use explicit idempotency keys for provider-bound attempts.
Provider webhook redelivery must be idempotent before any live provider integration is considered production-ready.

contactAttemptContract.name: InsuranceContactAttempt
rules: attemptId is canonical River-owned identity.
relationshipId must be canonical RiverCrmRelationshipId.
Provider identifiers may never replace attemptId or relationshipId.
triggerEventId may associate the attempt with an existing callback-requested relationship event.
idempotencyKey is River-owned and required before any provider invocation.
provider and providerReference remain optional until an adapter actually returns provider identity.
Lifecycle timestamps must match the attempt state.
Failure details may appear only for failed attempts.
retryable is meaningful only for a failed provider/orchestration result.
No raw provider payload is stored on the canonical attempt.
Terminal attempts are immutable except through explicitly designed reconciliation rules.
A failed attempt is not silently reset to queued; a retry creates or explicitly derives a separately governed attempt.
No state may be skipped merely because a provider uses different terminology; provider statuses must be normalized.
Provider webhook ordering must not regress a terminal attempt to an earlier lifecycle state.

requiredChecks: requested channel exists in canonical contactChannels
rules: Eligibility is deterministic and provider-neutral.
Unknown, denied, revoked, or missing consent is not eligible.
Eligibility does not infer legal permission beyond canonical River consent facts.
Provider invocation is impossible through the orchestration service when eligibility is denied.
The core orchestrator depends only on the interface.
Provider adapter owns HTTP/network transport.
Provider adapter maps provider-specific responses into canonical result shape.
Provider failure must distinguish retryable from deterministic failure.
The provider receives the River idempotency key whenever the provider supports idempotency.
Secrets and account credentials are provider-adapter runtime concerns and never part of InsuranceContactAttempt.
ProviderReference is optional canonical evidence, not River identity.
The same attempt must not intentionally initiate provider transport twice.
Provider invocation receives a stable attempt idempotency key.
Webhook/provider-event ingestion must maintain durable provider-event redelivery idempotency.
A retryable failure does not justify blindly replaying an attempt without explicit retry orchestration.
Provider event identifiers remain external references.

providerEventReceipt.decision: INS-002B must determine whether a small provider-event receipt table is necessary before INS-002F; if introduced, it must remain provider-neutral and use provider + provider_event_id as the durable dedupe key.
providerEventReceipt.purpose: Prevent webhook redelivery from applying one provider lifecycle update multiple times.

orchestrationSequence: Receive canonical InsuranceGrowthIntegrationContext and contact intent.
Evaluate channel eligibility before any provider work.
Create canonical queued InsuranceContactAttempt with River-owned attemptId and idempotencyKey.
Persist queued attempt before provider invocation.
Transition and persist attempt to attempting.
On provider acceptance, preserve providerReference without changing River identity.
Normalize synchronous provider state where available.
On provider failure, persist structured failure code/message/retryability.
Use later authenticated provider webhook reconciliation for asynchronous connected/completed/failed lifecycle outcomes.
Never fabricate provider success when persistence or transport fails.

rules: Private action must enforce same-origin semantics consistent with existing River CRM write actions.
Caller supplies canonical relationshipId and requested contact intent/channel only.
Caller must not supply attempt state, provider, providerReference, idempotency key, failure state, or arbitrary event metadata.
Server generates attemptId, eventId, idempotencyKey, and timestamps.
Server resolves canonical insurance context and consent before orchestration.
Callback intent persists canonical callback-requested event before associating the attempt.
Private ingress does not expose telephony provider credentials or raw provider payloads.
Provider-specific webhook route exists only after provider selection.
Signature verification occurs before normalization or persistence.
Exact raw request body is preserved when the chosen provider requires it for signature verification.
Provider event identity is durably deduplicated.
Provider statuses are normalized into InsuranceContactAttempt states.
Unknown provider statuses do not silently advance canonical state.
Provider event relationship is resolved through providerReference/attempt association, never by replacing canonical relationship identity.
Webhook redelivery must be safe.

acceptanceCriteria: INS-001 canonical relationship identity remains authoritative.
Callback-requested remains a canonical CRM trigger event rather than becoming the call state machine.
Contact attempts have River-owned canonical identities.
Consent and suppression are enforced before provider invocation.
Contact lifecycle state is durable and provider-neutral.
Provider references remain external evidence only.
Webhook redelivery can be made durably idempotent.
No vendor-specific type leaks into core orchestration contracts.
No Sesh schema, source, persistence, or runtime is changed.
Production resources are not mutated during local implementation unless separately authorized.
Repository-wide existing type debt is not broadened into INS-002.
